pages.text: "I'll only eat greens!" Mumu picked just the greens off the leaf plate, nudging the rice, corn, and tomatoes to its edge. Grandma watched quietly as she prepared the meal.
"I don't like mushy things." Mumu pushed the plate away. Only rice, corn, and tomatoes remained. Mumu bounded into the yard.
The next morning, Mumu stopped on the way to the well tree. One leg stretched forward, but the foot would not leave the ground. "Oh? My legs have no strength!"

Quick-handed monkey Taro came with a branch. "Let's hop across the stream stones!" Mumu's ears turned attentively, but their hind legs would not lift. Mumu sat down before the first stone. "My legs won't listen today."
Taro lay on Mumu's porch and looked at the leaf plate. Last night's rice, corn, and tomatoes were still there. "You only ate greens!"
Taro pointed to each food. "Rice for hopping, corn for sparkle, tomatoes for rosy cheeks, greens for strength! All four help your legs grow strong. Empty the Leaf Plate!"
Mumu took a bite of rice. "...Oh? It tastes nutty!" Mumu ate all the crunchy tomatoes, too, then picked up the last piece of corn.
The heavy hind legs felt light. Mumu bounded from the yard to the well tree's shade in one leap. Taro tapped twice with his branch. Tok-tok.
The next morning, Mumu sat before a fresh leaf plate, raised one finger, and ate a handful of greens first. "One, a bite of all four! Two, try what I haven't tried! Three, empty the plate!"
Grandma hugged Mumu. "Your legs have their strength back." Eating all four gave the legs growing strength. Mumu bounded up and called, "Taro, let's hop across stones today! Empty the Leaf Plate!"
